slot.brief: Solid floats at interface between two liquids with given fraction immersed; compare densities or find density of body

stem: A uniform solid block floats at the interface of two immiscible liquids of densities $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ ($\rho_1 < \rho_2$) with half of its volume in the upper liquid and half in the lower liquid. When the upper liquid is replaced by another immiscible liquid of density $2\rho_1$, the block floats with $\dfrac{3}{4}$ of its volume in the upper liquid. The ratio $\dfrac{\rho_2}{\rho_1}$ is:

verdicts.working: Buoyancy: block density ρb = (ρ1+ρ2)/2 from half-half flotation. After replacement: ρb = 2ρ1(3/4) + ρ2(1/4) = 1.5ρ1 + 0.25ρ2. Equating: 0.5ρ1+0.5ρ2 = 1.5ρ1+0.25ρ2 → ρ2 = 4ρ1. Check: ρb = 2.5ρ1 lies between 2ρ1 and 4ρ1, so interface flotation is consistent.

working:
Let $V$ be the volume and $\rho_b$ be the density of the block.

In the first equilibrium state:
$$V\rho_b g = \left(\dfrac{V}{2}\right)\rho_1 g + \left(\dfrac{V}{2}\right)\rho_2 g$$
$$\rho_b = \dfrac{1}{2}\rho_1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\rho_2 \quad \text{--- (1)}$$

In the second equilibrium state, the upper liquid has density $2\rho_1$, and $\dfrac{3}{4}$ of the volume is in the upper liquid (hence $\dfrac{1}{4}$ remains in the lower liquid of density $\rho_2$):
$$V\rho_b g = \left(\dfrac{3}{4}V\right)(2\rho_1) g + \left(\dfrac{1}{4}V\right)\rho_2 g$$
$$\rho_b = \dfrac{3}{2}\rho_1 + \dfrac{1}{4}\rho_2 \quad \text{--- (2)}$$

Equating (1) and (2):
$$\dfrac{1}{2}\rho_1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\rho_2 = \dfrac{3}{2}\rho_1 + \dfrac{1}{4}\rho_2$$
$$\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)\rho_2 = \left(\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\rho_1$$
$$\dfrac{1}{4}\rho_2 = \rho_1$$
$$\dfrac{\rho_2}{\rho_1} = 4$$

Independent check: Buoyancy: block density ρb = (ρ1+ρ2)/2 from half-half flotation. After replacement: ρb = 2ρ1(3/4) + ρ2(1/4) = 1.5ρ1 + 0.25ρ2. Equating: 0.5ρ1+0.5ρ2 = 1.5ρ1+0.25ρ2 → ρ2 = 4ρ1. Check: ρb = 2.5ρ1 lies between 2ρ1 and 4ρ1, so interface flotation is consistent.
